title: "Analyze Logs from a Data Pipeline"
description: "Record pipeline events with a run ID and context fields, then filter, summarize, export, and retain the logs using base R."
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Analyze Logs from a Data Pipeline}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}

---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE)
old_options <- options(width = 90)
old_level <- loggit2::set_log_level("DEBUG", confirm = FALSE)
old_calls <- loggit2::set_call_options(confirm = FALSE)
```

You want to answer questions such as: which run warned, which input was involved,
and how many rows were processed? Add named fields to a single `loggit()` call,
then read the file as a data frame. No separate schema or analysis package is
required.

## Start with one event

```{r first-event}
logfile <- tempfile(fileext = ".ndjson")

loggit2::loggit(
  "INFO", "Import completed",
  run_id = "demo-001", input_file = "input.csv", rows = 120L,
  logfile = logfile, echo = FALSE
)

loggit2::read_logs(logfile)[c("log_lvl", "log_msg", "run_id", "rows")]
```

Each call records an event with a timestamp, level and message. Each named custom
field becomes a column when the log is read. `loggit()` does not signal a
condition, even if you use level `"WARN"` or `"ERROR"`.

## Connect events from the same run

Use a consistent `run_id` to connect events and add fields where they are useful:

```{r pipeline-events}
loggit2::loggit(
  "WARN", "Empty values found",
  run_id = "demo-001", input_file = "input.csv", missing_rows = 3L,
  logfile = logfile, echo = FALSE
)
loggit2::loggit(
  "INFO", "Import completed",
  run_id = "demo-002", input_file = "next.csv", rows = 95L,
  logfile = logfile, echo = FALSE
)

events <- loggit2::read_logs(logfile)
events[c("log_lvl", "log_msg", "run_id", "rows", "missing_rows")]
```

Fields need not be present in every event. Missing fields become `NA`. Prefer a
small set of stable names such as `run_id`, `step` and `input_file`, with named
atomic values of length one. Longer vectors can multiply log rows; lists and
nested objects are not the intended field format. `timestamp` and `log_call` are
reserved; do not replace the standard level or message fields either.

## Understand the values you read

The file is NDJSON: one JSON object per line. Non-missing field values are stored
as JSON strings, including numeric and logical values. `read_logs()` consequently
returns character columns:

```{r field-types}
is.character(events$rows)
rows <- as.integer(events$rows)
sum(rows, na.rm = TRUE)
```

Convert fields explicitly when you want to calculate with them. `NA` is written
as JSON `null` and read back as `NA`. A field omitted from an event is also `NA`
in the data frame, so these two cases cannot be distinguished there.

## Find the run that needs attention

Use ordinary data-frame operations to filter and summarize:

```{r analyze-events}
warnings <- events[events$log_lvl == "WARN", ]
warnings[c("run_id", "input_file", "log_msg")]

table(events$log_lvl)
events[events$run_id == "demo-001", c("log_lvl", "log_msg")]
```

For the most recent entries first, read with `last_first = TRUE`:

```{r newest-first}
recent <- loggit2::read_logs(logfile, last_first = TRUE)
head(recent[c("run_id", "log_msg")], 1L)
```

This changes the row order of the returned data frame, not the file.

## Export for another tool

```{r csv-export}
csv_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
loggit2::convert_to_csv(csv_file, logfile = logfile)
utils::read.csv(csv_file)[c("run_id", "log_lvl", "log_msg")]
```

`convert_to_csv()` forwards additional arguments to `utils::write.csv()`.
It defaults to `unsanitize = FALSE`, preserving escaped special characters such
as `\n` inside values. `read_logs()` defaults to `unsanitize = TRUE`, restoring
them. Choose deliberately if messages contain line breaks and your downstream
tool expects one physical line per record.

## Keep only recent entries

To keep the last two entries in this example:

```{r retain-events}
loggit2::rotate_logs(2L, logfile = logfile)
loggit2::read_logs(logfile)[c("run_id", "log_msg")]
```

Rotation truncates the current file. It does not create an archive or run on a
schedule; decide when to call it from your application. To clear the log:

```{r clear-events}
loggit2::rotate_logs(0L, logfile = logfile)
nrow(loggit2::read_logs(logfile))
```

To capture conditions from a function without adding explicit events, see
[Log Existing Code in One Call](logging-existing-code.html). To choose a
persistent file or adjust levels, see
[Configure Logging and Understand Scope](further_configurations.html).

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
loggit2::set_log_level(old_level, confirm = FALSE)
loggit2::set_call_options(.arg_list = old_calls, confirm = FALSE)
options(old_options)
unlink(c(logfile, csv_file))
```
